task.title: Regression: slugify keeps separator runs and edge hyphens
task.statement: Regression report for slugkit.slugify(text). Since the last change the function returns 'hello--world' for 'Hello--World', 'a---b' for 'a -- b' and 'end-' for 'end!'. The intended behaviour, which the existing tests only partly cover, is: lower-case the text; every maximal run of one or more characters that are not ASCII letters a-z or ASCII digits 0-9 becomes exactly one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are removed; an input with no ASCII letters or digits (including the empty string and whitespace-only text) returns ''. Non-ASCII letters such as 'é' are separators, not kept characters (so 'café crème' is 'caf-cr-me'). Keep raising TypeError for non-string input, keep returning a str, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing without modifying them. Fix the regression in slugkit/core.py.
acceptance_criteria: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', slugify('(parens)') == 'parens' (no leading or trailing hyphen).
slugify('') == '', slugify('!!!') == '', slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).

Existing behaviour is preserved: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug', slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3', slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'.
Non-ASCII letters are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' and slugify('日本語') == ''.
The result is a str; TypeError for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'] and b'bytes'.

interface_contract.name: slugify
interface_contract.behavior: Convert the input string to a URL-friendly slug: 1) Lowercase the entire string. 2) Replace each maximal contiguous sequence of characters that are not ASCII letters (a-z) or ASCII digits (0-9) with a single hyphen ('-'). 3) Remove any leading or trailing hyphens from the result. 4) If the resulting string contains no ASCII letters or digits (i.e., it is empty or only hyphens), return the empty string. Non-ASCII letters (e.g., 'é', '日') are considered separators and are replaced by hyphens. The function returns a string.
error_cases: TypeError: raised if the input `text` is not an instance of str (e.g., None, int, float, list, bytes).

acceptance_criteria: 1. slugify('Hello--World') returns 'hello-world' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
2. slugify('a -- b') returns 'a-b' (spaces and multiple hyphens collapse).
3. slugify('one , two ; three') returns 'one-two-three' (punctuation and spaces collapse).
4. slugify('x___y') returns 'x-y' (underscore runs collapse).

7. slugify('--both--') returns 'both' (leading/trailing hyphens removed).

9. slugify('') returns '' (empty input yields empty string).

11. slugify('   ') returns '' (whitespace-only yields empty string).
12. slugify('Hello World') returns 'hello-world' (existing behavior preserved).

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter then classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, corrects and re-verifies them (must pass on the candidate and still fail on the base). Arbitration is advisory by default and never clears an implementation bug or a contract dispute; it changes the verdict only in explicit apply mode.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.
